question.text: In a 'Unified Structure', offshore and domestic capital are pooled at which level?

answer.text: At a Mauritius pooling vehicle only.
At a Singapore feeder fund only.
At the onshore Indian AIF (foreign investors route through automatic FDI into the Indian AIF).
Each investor invests directly in Indian investee companies.

explanation.text: The Logic: In a Unified Structure, all capital (offshore + domestic) is pooled at the Indian onshore AIF. Foreign investors flow in via FDI automatic route. Management and performance fees are charged at the Indian AIF level. No separate offshore pooling. The Trap: Mauritius-only describes pure offshore. Singapore-only describes master-feeder. Direct-investment describes parallel structure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C comparative table. XIX-D tests the manager's preference for unified (single fee stream) vs parallel. Manager's Pro-Tip: Unified structure is the simplest for the manager (single IM, single PPM), but some offshore LPs want their own feeder for tax efficiency - offer unified as default, feeder as bespoke.
